bottleneck: The gut microbiome influences immunity, metabolism, and even neurology, but engineering it is guesswork: introduced strains are outcompeted by residents, horizontal gene transfer scrambles designs, and the ecosystem's dynamics resist predictive modeling. Fecal transplants work for C. difficile yet remain crude, undefined consortia with variable composition. Rational microbiome design is still more aspiration than method, and engraftment of engineered strains is unreliable even in controlled studies.
current_state: Defined bacterial consortia are entering trials, and engineered probiotics show proof of concept, but durable engraftment and predictable function remain elusive. The field is still learning the ecology.
title: Microbiome engineering defies ecological prediction
why_it_blocks: A second genome — the microbiome — shapes human health, yet we cannot program it. Until engineered microbes reliably colonize and behave, microbiome medicine stays limited to crude transplants with unpredictable effects.
